about: What each preset of Invoke-DreamGUITests.ps1 runs. The runner owns this list; nothing here depends on the engine's ini groups.

A preset selects declared tests with any of: include (name prefixes), sources (directories under Source/DreamGUITests/ the test is declared in), flags (EAutomationTestFlags it must all carry); each criterion given narrows the selection, and exclude (name prefixes) then removes. sourcescan.py turns the selection into the shortest 'Automation RunTests' filter that matches exactly those tests. A preset may instead give a literal engine filter in "filter".

args are appended to the editor's command line. Under -nullrhi the engine itself drops every test flagged NonNullRHI (AutomationTest.cpp, GetValidTestNames), so a headless preset never needs to exclude the pixel tests.

minTests is the floor on the number of tests that must actually run; below it the run is an infrastructure failure (exit 2), which is how a plugin that loaded without its test module stops passing for green. Floors only go up. timeoutMinutes bounds one editor run; the build is not timed.
budgets: tests of the interactionPreset slower than interactionSlowMs, and any test slower than slowMs, are listed in the summary. They are reported, never failed.

Quick.about: The whole headless suite: every DreamGUI and DreamTween test that runs without a GPU, except the PIE layer. What the pre-push hook runs.

Interaction.about: The driver-level tests: everything declared under Private/Interaction and Private/Driver/Tests (the driver's own tests and the controls driven through it), headless.

Exit.about: The exit path (S9): a designer opened and closed, a preview shut down twice and a play session started and stopped, then an editor exit the way a person makes one -- the automation SoftQuit, not -TestExit's forced exit -- with the log searched afterwards for what a teardown must never leave (the lifecycle probe I7). In its own editor, out of Quick.

PieRhi.about: The play-in-editor layer's NonNullRHI tests, which -nullrhi drops from Pie: a play session drawn on a real RHI that renders off screen, for what needs Slate to lay its viewport out or the renderer to fill it. The picture of a play session's viewport is written to Saved/DreamGUITests/Captures.

Designer.about: The widget blueprint designer, headless. Its pixel scenarios (DreamGUI.Designer.RHI) are NonNullRHI and run in Rhi instead.

Rhi.about: Every test flagged NonNullRHI except the PIE layer's (each PIE test first replaces the editor's level with a blank map, which the pixel tests draw through) and the benchmark's (Perf), on a real RHI that renders off screen (no window). Every picture a test holds to a golden image is written to Saved/DreamGUITests/Captures.

Validate.about: The Rhi preset under the RHI validation layer, which turns missing transitions and stale bindings into deterministic asserts with a callstack instead of a timing-dependent crash.

Perf.about: The benchmark (DreamGUI.Performance.*) alone in its editor on a real RHI off screen, so that nothing else competes for the machine while it is timed. It writes Saved/DreamGUITests/Perf/Benchmark.json and a CPU trace, Benchmark.utrace; Tools/Tests/perf_report.py shows, compares and breaks them down. Nothing fails on a time: a number is only worth something next to another run's on the same machine.

Pie.about: The play-in-editor layer (DreamGUI.Pie.*): a real game mode, local player, viewport and viewport client, one PIE session per test. In its own editor, out of Quick. Its NonNullRHI tests are dropped under -nullrhi and run in PieRhi.

All.about: Everything in one editor: the headless suite, the PIE layer and the NonNullRHI tests, on a real RHI that renders off screen. GPU Scene's reserved buffers are off here (-dpcvars): every test world's scene reserves 8 GiB of GPU address space for them (GPUScene.cpp, four 2 GiB buffers), a destroyed world keeps its scene until the next garbage collection (a minute apart in the editor), and a hundred test worlds in five seconds ran the process out of address space -- D3D12 removed the device (DXGI_ERROR_DRIVER_INTERNAL_ERROR) on the next 2 GiB reservation. Without reserved resources the same buffers are ordinary ones sized to what each scene holds.
